chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Ajwa is the mother of the dates which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down to Adam (peace be upon him) from Paradise.

key_terms.أُمُّ التَّمْرِ: Mother of the dates, indicating the origin or primary variety.
key_terms.الْعَجْوَةُ: Ajwa, a specific variety of dates, considered superior and blessed.
key_terms.لآدَمَ: To Adam, the first Prophet and human.
key_terms.مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ: From Paradise, indicating the celestial origin of the fruit.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Ajwa dates in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi identifies the Ajwa date as the specific variety sent down to Prophet Adam (peace be upon him) from Paradise, establishing a unique theological link between the first human and this fruit. In Shia scholarly tradition, this narrative underscores the Ajwa's primordial origin and medicinal virtues, often cited to highlight the spiritual and physical benefits of consuming dates from Medina. The report elevates the Ajwa beyond a mere food source to a symbol of divine sustenance and healing.
